pr_title: Refactor ruleset skin transforming logic to be per-`ISkin` rather than one `ISkinSource`
pr_body:
Closes #13403

PR'ing this as a proof-of-concept for the forward direction of ruleset skin transformers, which is that each transformer would now only be responsible for transforming one `ISkin`, rather than taking the full `ISkinSource` and passing raw `ISkin`s returned by `FindProvider` to skin components, which appeared to have violated the idea of ruleset transformers as can be seen in the [linked issue](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/13403).

This PR blindly went through each transformer and replaced all calls to `FindProvider` with just using `this`/`Skin` instead, I still haven't thoroughly tested whether this is behaving correctly for all rulesets yet, but they should theoretically all be correct.

- #### https://github.com/ppy/osu/commit/6538d44708646a2b32b4aa0b112d7d31d82d38ff (`SkinProvidingContainer.SkinSources`)

  `SkinProvidingContainer` will now be able to perform lookups on multiple `ISkin`s before falling back to a parent `ISkinSource`, that'll make things straightforward for `RulesetSkinProvidingContainer` to surround each `SkinManager` skin provider with the ruleset skin transformer.

- #### https://github.com/ppy/osu/commit/33a9cac398f446bb01b5e9e9bd9463f81edd62ae (`RulesetSkinProvidingContainer`)

  Adds a special type of `SkinProvidingContainer` that takes the beatmap skin and all of `SkinManager`'s individual skin layers and plugs the ruleset skin transformer to them.

#### Notes

- One downside about `RulesetSkinProvidingContainer` is that it only specifically provides the `SkinManager` skin providers/layers, so if there was a test that caches an `ISkinSource` on top of `Player` for skin testing purposes, it will just be ignored from now onwards.
  
  An alternative to `RulesetSkinProvidingContainer` would be to actually do the transforming logic at `SkinManager` since it is an `ISkinSource` itself. But that still doesn't fully solve the issue as then any `ISkinSource` that's cached on top of `Player` in tests would have to somehow surround themselves with the ruleset transformer to achieve correct results.

  Open for feedback/discussion, I think the current way is good enough, `PlayerTestScene` can make some way for overriding the `Player`'s skin setup and passing arbitrary skins instead.

  - [x] Update tests which were relying on this `ISkinSource` caching quirk with the above method, unless we go an alternative way. (blocked for that)
pr_comments: I'm not sure where the `Layers` term comes from but let's avoid arbitrarily adding new terminology. You can just call it `SkinSources` instead no? Or just `Sources` or `CurrentSources` since the `Skin` part is implied most of the time.

>   An alternative to `RulesetSkinProvidingContainer` would be to actually do the transforming logic at `SkinManager` since it is an `ISkinSource` itself. But that still doesn't fully solve the issue as then any `ISkinSource` that's cached on top of `Player` in tests would have to somehow surround themselves with the ruleset transformer to achieve correct results.

This can't be a thing. There's both no way the game can known which ruleset is required (since the `Player` instance may modify it) not *should* it know.

If this is of a concern, then the skin "layers" aka sources should not be returned from `SkinManager` in the first place. It should be up to `Player` or `RulesetSkinProvidingContainer` to have that logic (ie. exposing the `DefaultSkin` and `DefaultLegacySkin` from `SkinManager` and conditionally consuming them locally). May be worth giving a try to avoid the weird list exposure you've added, which I'm weakly against as it's a point-in-time snapshot that doesn't follow bindable changes. This would feel better if it's only done in a very private context, alongside the `SourceChanged` handling for changes.

> I'm not sure where the `Layers` term comes from but let's avoid arbitrarily adding new terminology. You can just call it `SkinSources` instead no? Or just `Sources` or `CurrentSources` since the `Skin` part is implied most of the time.

I was just not completely fine about using the term `Source` because, well, it's not an `ISkinSource`, but I guess it's not that much of a problem?

Not sure. Maybe a bit weird using `Sources` but I don't have a better suggestion. `SkinsForLookup` or something? I'm not sure the conflict with `ISkinSource` in naming is that bad even, because in this case they are basically being consumed for the same premise.

All tests should be fixed and even more simplified now! Using the new `PlayerTestScene.GetPlayerSkin` method, which would accept an arbitrary `ISkin` passed by the test scene and puts it in the `RulesetSkinProvidingContainer`'s `SkinSources` as the most prioritized one over the `SkinManager` skins (`Insert(0, skin)` basically). However, I've noticed `TestSceneSkinEditor.TestToggleEditor` failing once (out of million attempts afterwards) due to a collection mutation attempt while iterating it here in `SkinProvidingContainer`: I'm suspecting this has to do with the fact that `SkinSources` gets cleared in `Dispose` (which is executed in a different async disposal thread), and that could result in such exception if a `GetDrawableComponent` call is in progress. Therefore I've removed that and went with direct unbinding instead here in this commit (https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/13423/commits/2240e2c39c7b1bf3ebe846b3d8c40119086b0e58).
Ruleset template tests have failed here (!). Probably worth taking a look as it may indicate a ruleset API change at best and actual breakage at worst.
Fixed, just handled the case where `CreateLegacySkinProvider` returns null, should be good now hopefully.

Going to merge this in tentatively because i'm done with this PR. I *think* this results in a much better state of affairs.

We can deal with any fallout post-merge.

issue_context.title: Legacy slider ball doesn't get correct skin colour
issue_context.body:
Due to the new provider lookup logic, the colour lookup is now being performed without a surrounding `OsuLegacySkinTransformer`, which was responsible for mapping the ruleset-specific colour lookups.

This has also potentially regressed other cases where the transformers are mutating the lookup (even in `GetSamples` cases for instance). A proposed fix is to ensure every `ISkin` is wrapped in its own transformer, rather than shoving one at the top of the `ISkinSource` lookup chain. @frenzibyte is going to look into that.

review_comments: Seems a bit weird that this call specifically is not calling on `Skin` but `this`. Might want to add a note here if that's done for a specific reason.

More like best practice in transformers, if you're calling a method that's not this method, then call it with `this`, otherwise call `Skin`.

A bit of confusing one, but that's that. And not sure if a note is worth really.

So the defining factor here is that all the other calls in this method are to `GetDrawableComponent` rather than some other method?

Is it feasible to change them to `base.` calls instead and have the forwarding to `Skin.Get...` there? It might read better.

I've applied the changes proposed here (https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/13423/commits/fbb856d84bfdfb2e5c4c5ee3fbfde90302864000). Interestingly though, previously some transformers were not calling `base.GetSample` and instead calling `Skin.GetSample` directly, this makes them skip certain logic in the base sample lookup method regarding overriding layered hit samples with virtual samples if they're turned off in skin settings...

I guess it's more correct now? might have to check stable for this one.
Since this is doing quite dangerous stuff (binding to external events), I'd like to see the rest of the switch cases handled, such as `Reset` and `Replace`.
I was always wondering why some usages don't handle all cases other than `Add` and `Remove`, but TIL.
Any reason this isn't combined with the other calls above?
Explained in the comment that's exactly above the lines you highlighted, basically `DrawableRuleset` and storyboard need to be fully loaded before calling `createOverlayComponents`.
I intentionally haven't exposed this as `Skin`s as that allows them to be mutated outside of here, I guess it's fine?

This is very weird to me, because something like `c.FindProvider(s => s.GetTexture(...) != null)` is actually going to iterate through `SkinSources` twice. Once in here and once inside the `lookupFunction`.

It seems like this iteration may not be required?
Also it's not actually consuming the `skin` here..

Whoops... this actually needs some work, I was hoping i could get rid of `FindProvider` but looks like that's not happening anytime soon. (~~with animations and taiko mascot animations being the most blocking one~~ actually this could just be replaced with a `GetDrawableComponent` lookup that's simplified in the `GetAnimation` extension, will keep thinking about this)

Resolved with a refactor of this disability logic, now the allow checks are performed on a private `DisableableSkinSource` and all lookups in `SkinProvidingContainer` are forwarded to them (which includes `FindProvider` which now does `lookupFunction(disableableSkinSource[skin])`).

Same here, I would actually like to see the event unbound from the list, just so that shenanigans don't occur if the list is changed after disposal.

Note also that this is effectively the same as just clearing the list.

Probably needed to write a comment, but doing this may actually cause a "collection was modified; enumeration operation may not execute" exception due to the disposal being on a separate thread (at least that's what I had speculated from the test failure I reported above this review)

Weird having only `Ruleset` in the name when it's also handling the beatmap.

Also is it feasible to just pass in the `WorkingBeatmap` rather than the two separate components of it?

Not sure, two separate `WorkingBeatmap`s are used in usages so I wasn't sure about doing that.

As for the name, yeah, I'm not sure, I chose `Ruleset` because it is the most benefited area with this container, maybe `Gameplay`? not sure if it's fine to have a "`Gameplay`" component in editor though
Ruleset is better than Gameplay. Let's just go with it for now.
